name: alakazam741_v10_route_eta
archetype: Alakazam 741 top-8 core — v9 state machine + route/backup-ETA refinements
summary: v9 top-8 core (turn state machine + attack reservation + dynamic deck model) with seven targeted decision fixes: reachable-Alakazam complete-route test, energy-aware backup_eta, route-deficit Poké Pad, board-deficit Dawn/Hilda selection, mirror-only pre-attack Xerosic, one-per-turn Night Stretcher, and need-gated Battle Cage. Same 60 cards as v8/v9; no Boss's Orders and no opponent-card/deck-name matchup branches.
notes: Deck is byte-identical to alakazam741_v9_top8_core / alakazam741_v8 — v10 isolates the LOGIC change only.
_holds_complete_route requires a reachable attacking Alakazam (Abra + Kadabra/Candy + Alakazam card + fuel), so Lillie is no longer suppressed by an incomplete hand.
_has_backup_line replaced by energy-aware _backup_eta; only backup_eta<=1 is a sufficient follow-up; _backup_energy_short prioritises energy over extra development.
Poké Pad fetches by route deficit and never fetches Alakazam while no Abra exists to build under it.
Dawn vs Hilda chosen from the board deficit, not a fixed point gap.
Xerosic is mirror-only and only as a pre-attack disruption; never in LOCKED and never as the sole turn-ending action.
Night Stretcher capped at one use per turn unless a second directly makes a KO now or secures the next attacker.
Battle Cage gated on a genuine bench-protection need; the pre-attack gate prevents it from costing the current KO.

Unchanged from v9: PRESSURE attack priority, Dudunsparce base Tier + deck model, attack-instead-of-END, minimal manual retreat, last-body Dudunsparce safety, 0-damage Powerful Hand guard, 60-card deck.
